opportunities.title: Synthesis grants

amount.raw: Synthesis groups can claim up to £30,000 over two years for groups of 8-15 participants.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Main applicant must have BES membership; groups of 8-15 individuals from diverse interdisciplinary backgrounds across universities, research institutes, NGOs, industry and government departments.
opportunities.summary: Funds the formation of new two-year synthesis groups that bring together diverse interdisciplinary groups to focus on data analysis and synthesis, fostering collaboration and mentoring. Round 2 of 2026.

opportunities.title: Long-term research grants

amount.raw: £3,500 in year 1 (first five years' funding), averaging £500/year; additional £3,500 in year 6 after satisfactory report.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to all types of ecologists including conservation practitioners (e.g. Reserve Managers, consultants) and university academics; awarded to individuals not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Provides funding over 10 years to enable existing short-term projects with 1-2 years of data to be funded into the long term, supporting long-term ecological studies anywhere in the world. Round 2 of 2026.

opportunities.title: Pedagogical research and development grants

amount.raw: Projects can be awarded up to £5,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level (early years to life-long learning in formal or informal settings); awarded to individuals not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Funds research informing teaching and learning practices that improve learners' experience and promote excellence in teaching ecology, producing evidence-based examples and recommendations. Round 2 of 2026.

opportunities.title: Connecting ecologists with other disciplines grants

amount.raw: Grant awards of up to £20,000 can be claimed from the applicant.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations; undergraduates and masters students not eligible; awarded to individuals not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Funds interdisciplinary secondments/placements (up to 12 months) that immerse an ecologist in another professional world (another discipline, NGO, public sector, business) to develop interdisciplinary skills. Round 2 of 2026.

opportunities.title: Small research grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; researchers from all countries globally; projects conducted anywhere in the world; not for completion of undergraduate/masters degrees or funded fellowships.
opportunities.summary: Funds new and innovative ecological research of the highest international standard with a clear ecological science focus. Round 2 of 2026.

opportunities.title: Outreach and engagement grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicant must have BES membership; open to individuals, teams and organisations across all experience levels; projects aimed at non-academic audiences.
opportunities.summary: Funds independent outreach, public engagement and science communication activities that engage public audiences with the excitement, importance and relevance of ecological science. Round 2 of 2026.

opportunities.title: Training and travel grants

amount.raw: Maximum £500 for in-person events; maximum £250 for virtual conferences/courses.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member and a PhD student or postgraduate researcher; not open to postdocs, undergraduates or masters students; work/study at a university or research institution.
opportunities.summary: Helps PhD students and postgraduate researchers meet the costs of specialist field training courses and travel associated with presenting work at workshops and conferences. Third 2026 round opens 24 August and closes 8 September 2026.

opportunities.title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member at any career stage; must be a citizen of and based in the Global South; must have applied to present at the Annual Meeting; must be at least three years since last BES Training and Travel Grant.
opportunities.summary: Supports researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting 2026 in the UK, covering travel and related costs. Open 17 July to 8 September 2026.
